001package io.github.ai4ci.config.inhost;
002
003import org.immutables.value.Value;
004
005import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeInfo;
006import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeName;
007import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonDeserialize;
008import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonSerialize;
009
010import io.github.ai4ci.abm.Outbreak;
011import io.github.ai4ci.config.execution.DemographicAdjustment;
012import io.github.ai4ci.config.execution.ExecutionConfiguration;
013import io.github.ai4ci.functions.Distribution;
014import io.github.ai4ci.functions.SimpleDistribution;
015
016/**
017 * Configuration for an in‑host Markov state model.
018 *
019 * <p>
020 * This interface describes the distributions and parameters used by the
021 * simplistic in‑host Markov model implementation. It supplies distributions for
022 * incubation, infectious and symptom durations, and for the immune waning
023 * half‑life. Implementations are primarily consumed by the initialiser and
024 * state classes that set up and manage an individual's in‑host state.
025 *
026 * <p>
027 * Downstream uses include the initialisers and builders such as
028 * {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultInHostMarkovStateInitialiser},
029 * {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultPersonInitialiser} and
030 * {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultInHostPhenomenologicalStateInitialiser}.
031 * It is also referenced by example and test code such as
032 * {@link io.github.ai4ci.example.Experiment}.
033 *
034 * @author Rob Challen
035 */
036@Value.Immutable
037@JsonSerialize(as = ImmutableMarkovStateModel.class)
038@JsonDeserialize(as = ImmutableMarkovStateModel.class)
039@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)
040@JsonTypeName("markov")
041public interface MarkovStateModel extends InHostConfiguration,
042                DemographicAdjustment.Markov<Distribution, Double> {
043
044        /**
045         * A sensible default parameterisation of the Markov model.
046         *
047         * <p>
048         * This instance provides a small set of log‑normal distributions used as a
049         * baseline in examples and tests. Downstream callers that rely on a simple
050         * default include {@link io.github.ai4ci.example.Experiment}.
051         *
052         * @see io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultInHostMarkovStateInitialiser
053         */
054        ImmutableMarkovStateModel DEFAULT = ImmutableMarkovStateModel.builder()
055                .setDescription(
056                        "A SEIR like in host model with incubation period ~ 5 days, infectious duration ~ 8 days, symptom duration ~ 5 days, and immunity ~ 300 days.",
057                        "The viral load is derived from the severity which is calibrated from the overall outbreak parameters"
058                )
059                .setImmuneWaningHalfLife(SimpleDistribution.logNorm(300D, 10D))
060                .setIncubationPeriod(SimpleDistribution.logNorm(5D, 2D))
061                .setInfectiousDuration(SimpleDistribution.logNorm(8D, 3D))
062                .setSymptomDuration(SimpleDistribution.logNorm(5D, 3D))
063                .build();
064
065        /**
066         * Distribution for the half life of waning immunity.
067         *
068         * <p>
069         * This distribution describes the expected time scale for immune waning and
070         * is sampled when determining the decay of immunity after recovery or
071         * vaccination. It is consulted by initialisers and state updaters. The
072         * distribution is not age specific in this model but may be modified by
073         * {@link DemographicAdjustment.Markov} implementations that provide
074         * age‑specific adjustments to the symptom duration distribution in the form
075         * of an odds ratio.
076         *
077         * @return a {@link io.github.ai4ci.functions.Distribution} representing the
078         *         immune waning half life
079         */
080        @Override
081        Distribution getImmuneWaningHalfLife();
082
083        /**
084         * Distribution for the incubation period (time from infection to onset).
085         *
086         * <p>
087         * This distribution is sampled by initialisers such as
088         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultInHostMarkovStateInitialiser}
089         * and by phenomenological initialisers when converting to internal state
090         * durations. It is not age specific in this model but may be modified by
091         * {@link DemographicAdjustment.Markov} implementations that provide
092         * age‑specific adjustments to the incubation period distribution in the form
093         * of a odds ratio.
094         *
095         * @return a {@link io.github.ai4ci.functions.Distribution} used to sample
096         *         incubation periods
097         */
098        @Override
099        Distribution getIncubationPeriod();
100
101        /**
102         * Distribution for the infectious duration.
103         *
104         * <p>
105         * This value is not age specific in the current model. Callers include the
106         * default initialiser which samples an infectious duration for each infected
107         * individual. The distribution is not age specific in this model but may be
108         * modified by {@link DemographicAdjustment.Markov} implementations that
109         * provide age‑specific adjustments to the symptom duration distribution in
110         * the form of an odds ratio.
111         *
112         * @return a {@link io.github.ai4ci.functions.Distribution} for infectious
113         *         duration
114         */
115        @Override
116        Distribution getInfectiousDuration(); // not age specfic
117
118        /**
119         * Severity cutoff used to decide whether an infected individual is classed
120         * as fatal.
121         *
122         * <p>
123         * The default implementation derives the cutoff from the
124         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.config.execution.ExecutionConfiguration#getInfectionFatalityRate()}
125         * as 1 minus the fatality rate. This is used when mapping severity to death
126         * outcomes in the outbreak and state logic.
127         *
128         * @param outbreak      the current outbreak context
129         * @param configuration the execution configuration providing fatality rates
130         * @return the cutoff in the unit interval [0,1] used to classify fatality
131         */
132        @Override
133        default double getSeverityFatalityCutoff(
134                        Outbreak outbreak, ExecutionConfiguration configuration
135        ) {
136                return 1 - configuration.getInfectionFatalityRate();
137        }
138        // NB not modifiable at present
139
140        // The markov model has no internal representation of continuous severity
141        // and the cutoffs are arbitrary
142
143        /**
144         * Severity cutoff used to decide whether an infected individual is classed
145         * as hospitalised.
146         *
147         * <p>
148         * The default implementation derives the cutoff from the
149         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.config.execution.ExecutionConfiguration#getInfectionHospitalisationRate()}
150         * as 1 minus the hospitalisation rate. Downstream uses include the same
151         * baseline and state classes that interpret severity measures.
152         *
153         * @param outbreak      the current outbreak context
154         * @param configuration the execution configuration providing hospitalisation
155         *                      rates
156         * @return the cutoff in the unit interval [0,1] used to classify
157         *         hospitalisation
158         */
159        @Override
160        default double getSeverityHospitalisationCutoff(
161                        Outbreak outbreak, ExecutionConfiguration configuration
162        ) {
163                return 1 - configuration.getInfectionHospitalisationRate();
164        }
165        // NB not modifiable at present
166
167        /**
168         * Severity cutoff used to decide whether an infected individual is classed
169         * as a symptomatic case.
170         *
171         * <p>
172         * The default implementation derives the cutoff from the
173         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.config.execution.ExecutionConfiguration#getInfectionCaseRate()}
174         * as 1 minus the case rate. This method is used by classes such as
175         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.OutbreakBaseline},
176         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.PersonState} and
177         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultOutbreakBaseliner} to map a
178         * continuous severity measure to discrete outcomes.
179         *
180         * @param outbreak      the current outbreak context
181         * @param configuration the execution configuration providing attack rates
182         * @return the cutoff in the unit interval [0,1] used to classify symptoms
183         */
184        @Override
185        default double getSeveritySymptomsCutoff(
186                        Outbreak outbreak, ExecutionConfiguration configuration
187        ) {
188                return 1 - configuration.getInfectionCaseRate();
189        }
190        // NB not modifiable at present
191
192        /**
193         * Distribution for the duration of symptoms.
194         *
195         * <p>
196         * Used by initialisers to determine how long symptomatic states last. The
197         * distribution is not age specific in this model but may be modified by
198         * {@link DemographicAdjustment.Markov} implementations that provide
199         * age‑specific adjustments to the symptom duration distribution in the form
200         * of an odds ratio.
201         *
202         * @return a {@link io.github.ai4ci.functions.Distribution} for symptom
203         *         duration
204         */
205        @Override
206        Distribution getSymptomDuration(); // not age specfic
207
208}
